The fake-serialization defect is real and the published catalog is this lane's surface. Direction settled by the seat: **the published skill states the PROPERTY, not a repo-specific command** — the catalog ships into customer codebases where neither `/tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock` nor `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` exists, so any copy-pasteable literal is wrong-by-construction somewhere; the fix states the invariants (one shared heavy-verify lock per container; acquisition budget bounded inside one foreground call; queue-timeout distinguishable from command failure; hold duration observable) and defers the mechanism to the host repo's tooling, naming this repo's entry point only as an example of the shape. The `--force` worktree nit is in scope (align with the refusal-is-the-guard rule).
